Addressed in the `ranex` fork: `opencode upgrade`'s `releases/latest` fetch now resolves a GitHub token (`resolveTokenOptional`) and sends `Authorization: Bearer` when present; anonymous otherwise. Commit `db611eb18f` (`github-auth-module` branch). Same root cause as #36260 (these two look like duplicates).
Addressed in the `ranex` fork: `opencode upgrade` now resolves a GitHub token (`resolveTokenOptional`) and authenticates the `releases/latest` fetch. Commit `db611eb18f`. Duplicate of #23461.

Addressed in the `ranex` fork: the `install` script resolves `${GITHUB_TOKEN:-${GH_TOKEN}}` into a 0600 curl config file (kept out of argv / `ps`) and passes it to all GitHub curls; the version-fetch pipeline also no longer aborts under `set -e`+pipefail on a rate-limited response. Commit `db611eb18f`.

Addressed in the `ranex` fork: remote `instructions` URLs are fetched with a resolved bearer token for GitHub hosts (`github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `*.githubusercontent.com`, or a configured `GH_HOST`); non-GitHub and non-`https` URLs stay anonymous. `packages/ranex/src/session/instruction.ts`, commit `db611eb18f`.
Addressed in the `ranex` fork: the GitHub Action handler now reads the `AGENT` env var and passes it to `session.prompt` (previously ignored — always ran the default agent). Commit `c187ce9cbc`.

Addressed in the `ranex` fork: on `pull_request_review_comment` triggers, replies now use `pulls.createReplyForReviewComment` (in-thread) instead of a top-level PR comment, mirroring the existing reaction-routing branch. Commit `c187ce9cbc`.

Addressed in the `ranex` fork: `getLanguage`/`resolveSDK` now guard the provider lookup and return `ModelNotFoundError` (with catalog/fuzzysort suggestions) instead of crashing with `undefined is not an object` when a model's provider isn't registered. The reported `p.rest` token was from an older released binary; current source dereferences `.options`. Commit `2fa8fd30d5` (`provider-missing-guard` branch).

Addressed in the `ranex` fork (`plan-mode-bash-guard` branch, commit `de1e2e5618`): Plan mode now enforces a shell policy — prompt-by-default on bash, flat-deny of known mutating gh/git subcommands, deny of built-in GitHub writes (`*:write:*`), allowlist of common read-only commands. Best-effort, not a sandbox (documented). Same root cause as #34390.

Addressed in the `ranex` fork (`plan-mode-bash-guard`, commit `de1e2e5618`) — see comment on #34190: Plan mode now denies/ prompts on mutating gh/git/`curl` commands and built-in GitHub writes. Closes the `gh issue create`/`gh api` bypass.

Seconding the #40095 lead — opencode-go hangs when outbound connectivity stalls, and WSL's default NAT setup has flaky IPv6/DNS that produces exactly this "stream starts, never returns" pattern. Test with a plain `curl -v --max-time 10` to the gateway endpoint from inside WSL, and try disabling IPv6 on the interface (`sudo sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1`) or pinning a DNS server. If the curl stalls too, it's the WSL network layer, not the provider.

This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #23114: Same root cause — session title generation passes synthetic/injected memory parts through `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect`, causing titles to reflect plugin-injected context rather than the actual user message. The suggested fix direction is also identical (filter synthetic parts before building the title prompt).

Please review #23114 and consider closing this one in favor of it, or linking them if you believe there are distinct aspects worth tracking separately.

Duplicate of #23114 — same root cause, same suggested fix, and the comment by coryplastek there even uses the same workaround we applied locally (override the `title` agent model). Closing in favor of #23114 and adding our code-level findings there.

Code-level confirmation for v1.18.18 (path still identical on `dev` as of 2026-08-13):

- `SessionPrompt.ensureTitle` (`packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:193-253`) builds the title prompt from `history.slice(0, idx + 1)` via `MessageV2.toModelMessagesEffect(context, mdl)`.
- `toModelMessagesEffect` (`packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:206`) skips text parts only when `part.ignored` or empty — `synthetic` parts pass through:

```ts
if (part.type === "text" && !part.ignored && part.text !== "")
  userMessage.parts.push({ type: "text", text: part.text })
```

- Verified end-to-end: `opencode-mem` (`chat.message` hook, `injectOn: "first"`) prepends a synthetic memory part to the first user message; that part is persisted in `opencode.db` and flows into the title prompt. With a weak small_model the title blends memory text with the user's message (e.g. "Error en certificado Arreglo en sitio pepe SSL").

Re the concern that stripping everything would lose useful preloaded context (files, shell output): those are non-synthetic user/assistant parts and would remain — filtering only `synthetic: true` parts (or adding a `stripSynthetic` option alongside the existing `stripMedia`) would target exactly the plugin-injected context without dropping real content.

```bash
( cd /home/schnip-cstg/git/models.dev && bun install && bun run --cwd packages/web build )

git clone git@github.com:NachoFLizaur/opencode.git /home/schnip-cstg/git/opencode 2>/dev/null || true
git -C /home/schnip-cstg/git/opencode checkout feat/kiro-provider
( cd /home/schnip-cstg/git/opencode && bun install && bun run --cwd packages/opencode script/build.ts --single )

OPENCODE_MODELS_PATH="/home/schnip-cstg/git/models.dev/packages/web/dist/_api.json" /home/schnip-cstg/git/opencode/packages/opencode/dist/opencode-linux-x64/bin/opencode
```

Addressed in the ranex fork (ranex-trim): the shell tool now guards the parse-error / zero-command permission bypass. Root cause: a trailing double-dash (or other malformed input) makes tree-sitter-powershell emit an ERROR node with zero command descendants, and a clean-parse zero-command input (comment/redirection-only) also yields zero command nodes — so collect() produced empty scan.patterns and ask() early-returned before any permission rule was evaluated (beating configured deny AND ask). Fix: on tree.rootNode.hasError OR commands(root).length===0, replace the scan with the raw command so the permission check always fires; valid parses untouched. Commit 2d0950f6e5 (merged to ranex-trim). Supersedes the narrower hasError-only guard; applies upstream.

Addressed in the ranex fork (ranex-trim): tail()'s single-line byte-slice fallback was guarded by out.length===0, but a trailing newline makes split() push an empty sentinel first (out.length becomes 1 while bytes stays 0), so the real over-limit line was dropped and the tool returned (no output) instead of the truncated tail. Guard on bytes===0 instead, so the fallback fires whenever nothing has been accumulated by byte count. Hits any newline-terminated single-line output over the byte limit (cat of a minified bundle, jq -c, curl, base64). Commit 204757bd5a; adds a trailing-newline regression test. Approach applies upstream.

Partially addressed in the ranex fork (ranex-trim). (B) apply_patch: insertion-only chunks (empty oldLines) now insert at the changeContext anchor when set, or at EOF for endOfFile/no-anchor — instead of always appending at EOF (which ignored the anchor). The ranex parser also now reaches the End-of-File marker (a generic terminator previously made that branch unreachable). Adds 3 regression cases + a multi-chunk insertion-then-edit test. Commit 5c7bec8156. Both copies (core patch.ts + the ranex reimplementation) were fixed. I was able to resolve this issue by upgrading SecureCRT.

The problem was reproducible with:

* SecureCRT 9.6.x
* OpenCode 1.18.x
* SSH to Ubuntu
* `TERM=xterm-256color`

The OpenCode UI displayed repeated fragments such as:

```text
;w=1;▀;w=1;
```

I initially tested `OPENTUI_FORCE_EXPLICIT_WIDTH=0`, but this did not resolve the problem with the current OpenCode version.

The actual fix was upgrading SecureCRT to **9.7.x** (tested with **9.7.3**).

VanDyke's SecureCRT 9.7 changelog includes a relevant fix introduced in 9.7 Beta 4:

> If SecureCRT received unknown OSC escape sequences, the sequence may not have been ignored.

After upgrading SecureCRT, the latest OpenCode works correctly in the terminal over SSH. No OpenCode downgrade or Web UI workaround is required.

So this appears to have been a **SecureCRT terminal escape-sequence handling issue**, rather than an OpenCode rendering issue.

For anyone reproducing this with SecureCRT 9.6.x: upgrade to SecureCRT 9.7.x or newer.
